title: Notes of Ministry - 21 - August 1974

source.file: Various/Notes of Ministry - 21 - August 197 (2405)/Notes of Ministry - 21 - August - Various.epub

paragraphs.text: Most of us, I suppose, at some time or another in our lives have appreciated a word of counsel. Possibly the occasions on which we appreciated it were fewer than the occasions on which we needed it. Nevertheless through God’s grace we have been retained. Each of us at one time or another has been glad of a word of counsel, a word of exhortation, all intended to keep us in touch with God and in the path of His will. The Lord said when He was here,
“because lawlessness shall prevail, the love of the most shall grow cold”, Matthew 24: 12.

That has come to pass in our day. It may be argued that it refers to a day yet to come, and that is equally true, but we need to understand, dear brethren, that it has happened in our day that because iniquity is abounding the love of the most has waxed cold.

Some persons look for improvement; men in the world of certain religious beliefs regard leaven as good, something that will spread its influence throughout the world until the kingdom of Jesus Christ is supreme. That is not true. The fact is, the Scripture makes it abundantly plain that things will wax worse and worse. Persons looking for improvement publicly do not believe their Bible. That does not mean that we should be without encouragement. Sometimes we are apt to think that in the days of the apostle Paul things went forward publicly in a blaze of glory—that is not the truth either.
There was a time when Paul stood alone. What a dark day that was; “All who are in Asia …
have turned away from me”, 2 Timothy 1: 15. Was there a darker day than that? I think there was one darker day than that, when Jesus was crucified. But He had everything under

control—everything! We have often been reminded of the gospel of John where He takes the initiative when He was crucified. There is no reference either to the Father or to the Spirit, although they were there, but Jesus is the One who was in supreme command. How wonderful that is!

I think, dear brethren, the Lord would encourage us in a day of public darkness and weakness to listen to a word of counsel. It may come through an older brother; it may come through father or mother—often not too well received from that source—that is what I used to find when I was young anyway. But the word of counsel comes. I think the Lord would counsel us in these days to enter into a personal transaction with Himself what Mr. Raven has called
‘Christ’s last word of counsel’ appears in this passage.
Now before I speak of that I would like to refer to the Lord’s opening word: “And to the angel of the assembly in Laodicea, write”. Who is going to speak? One who calls Himself

“the Amen, the faithful and true witness, the beginning of the creation of God”. Is everything lost? Do you think everything is lost? One man of God once said that all is lost to those that say, All is lost. Is all lost, dear brethren? Again the same beloved man said, If the worst had not happened you would never have known from experience that He was equal to the worst.
The worst serves to bring out the glory of the Person who can handle the worst situation that ever arose in the history of the testimony. So it says,

“These things says the Amen”. Is not Laodicea the amen? Is not that the finish? Is that not the last phase of the assembly finishing in its responsibility? He is the Amen, and everything for God is secured in Him. Oh, dear brethren, we have the greatest reason for encouragement to go on. Everything is in His hands. Again it is said, “In him is the yea, and in him the amen”, 2 Corinthians 1: 20. All the promises of God are centred in Him.

So He addresses this assembly in its assumed riches but actual poverty—the Amen—now that is an encouragement to persons who desire to go on, to know that He is the First and the Last. He had the first word and He will have the last. What a Person He is! And then He says, “the faithful and true witness”. Why does He say that? Because it is maintained in Him; He is the “faithful and true witness”, and He brings it forward to the church which should have been a faithful and true witness but failed to be. So we find everything centred in the Person of Jesus.
Then, having introduced Himself thus, and as “the beginning of the creation of God”, He says, as to other assemblies, “I know thy works”, and I think He would address that to us.

You think of the beloved man that laboured in this city for so long, he said he always read the Bible as if it was addressed to himself. Do you read it like that? Or do you read it to acquire the word for somebody else? Another man who served long in his life said this—and I feel I should always myself be reminded of it, as well as reminding my brethren—one of the greatest dangers to any minister of the truth is supposing that what he says does not apply to himself but only to those to whom he speaks, as if to say, I am all right; you are the people who need the word. What a danger that is. So we stand together as listening to what the Lord has to say to us in a word of counsel—“I know thy works, that thou art neither cold nor hot”. You say, Does that apply to me? I have to take it home to myself; I know what the flesh is and I prefer the easy way. Do you not? Do not tell me that you do not, because you do: You prefer the easy way, and it is only love for Christ and the power of His love upon you that will cause you to take the path of discipleship.

So we accept the word, dear brethren, “I know thy works, that thou art neither cold nor hot; I would thou wert cold or hot”. How insipid christendom has become! He, says, ‘I wish you were one thing or the other’. Where are we, dear brethren, here tonight in this city? If you look around this city and throughout this country you see signs of affluence and material prosperity. Where do we stand as related to that? I am not saying that if God has prospered us we should not accept it in His government, because a rich man’s castle may be the wilderness to him and a poor man’s house or cottage may be his heaven. It is a question of your state of soul before God. So the question arises as the Lord speaks, How am I? He is going to make it a word of counsel to us, but first of all He discloses the awful state that exists. So He says, “Because thou art … neither cold nor hot, I am about to spue thee out of my mouth.” This is the church publicly. We say we understand the truth of it, that as looking at it in a simple prophetic way it is the final phase of the assembly’s history on earth, although the last four run concurrently. It is simple to say that and yet subtly to suppose that we are Philadelphia. Mr. Darby refers to that more subtle self.

The Lord would exercise us by this word. He says, “I counsel thee to buy of me gold purified by fire, that thou mayest be rich”. All this pretence that we are in the presence of, dear brethren! I am not suggesting that it is in the brethren here; we thank God for any that have escaped and whose bond is the truth. But a word of counsel is still needed. I recall the other word in Scripture also well known, “Buy the truth, and sell it not”, Proverbs 23: 23. The truth in our day has been shamefully sold for material advantage. Are you going to have a part in that? “I counsel thee to buy of me”. “Thee”—who is the thee? You say, The Lord is addressing the angel of the assembly in Laodicea. And who is that? Oh, we say, The responsible element. And who is that? Sometimes we speak of the responsible brothers in the locality. We like to sit back and put all the blame on them. It is a habit, you know. Those who do the least quite often have the most to say in criticism. Do not let us be like that, dear brethren.

So when the Lord says, “I counsel thee” I would like to ask you, Have you any responsibility in New York? Have I any responsibility in Gillingham? Every believer in this city has a responsibility. Remember this, the assembly has not lost its responsibility to Christ because it has failed. So, “I counsel thee”, the last word of counsel to the church is “to buy of me”. You can take that up. Persons say, We do not know. Whose fault is that? I may say, I do not know.

Whose fault is that? Are you prepared, beloved brother or sister, younger man or older man, to enter into a personal trading transaction with Jesus, with the One who is presenting Himself as the Amen, the faithful and true Witness? Or will you go along saying, I do not know? It casts a reflection on Him if you say that, because the resource is just as much available to you as it is to those who faithfully pursue the truth. I may fail in my responsibility, but that does not change or alter the resource. Our resource is in Him.

Here His word of counsel would meet us in dark and difficult days when things appear to be going from bad to worse. He counsels us to buy of Him gold tried by fire. How do we regard that? Well, you might say, we have had plenty of what appears to be fire in New York, plenty of troubles, trials, discipline. It may be needed! Peter says, “For a little while at present, if needed, put to grief by various trials”, 1 Peter 1: 6—if needed! They do not come if they are not needed. And the same thing would apply to us in our city, plenty of fire, or so we thought.

How many are prepared to purchase from Jesus? “Buy of me gold purified by fire”; and through your transaction with Him, whatever the discipline or sorrow through which you may pass, the glory of His work is to shine. “And white garments, that thou mayest be clothed”.

He wants us to be clothed, “that the shame of thy nakedness may not be made manifest”. The word is intended to come home to us. Christendom at large, alas, has no interest. I think the Lord would keep us alive by a word of prophecy.

Then He says, “and eye-salve … that thou mayest see”. There is a saying on our side of the water, and I expect you have it here, that there are none so blind as those who will not see. It may be true that certain persons cannot see, but He is available. He is available to the youngest person here, brother or sister, and you can enter into this trading transaction with Him personally. It will mean sacrifice. After all, if you walk into one of the shops in New York you do not get anything for nothing. In christianity in a certain sense you get everything for nothing, in another sense you get nothing for nothing, and I think we need to understand that. Who therefore is prepared to sacrifice in order to buy from the Lord Himself and be governed by the truth? The truth is really our bond. How we have failed in that! The truth is always the issue and the truth is our bond.
Then the Lord goes on to say, “Behold, I stand at the door and am knocking; if any one hear my voice and open the door, I will come in unto him and sup with him, and he with me”.

What a privilege that is! Do you think that is possible? I ask you, do you think we are dealing with philosophies or with realities? John Bunyan said, ‘I notice this, that these things are only for those persons who are in downright earnest’. Now, you young men and young women, are we dealing with philosophies or realities? Is christianity a revelation from God or is it a comparative philosophy? We are dealing with realities; we are having to do with God. This is a great privilege, and although to some persons it might be frightening, it is never intended to be.

The Lord says, “If any one … open the door”. Are you prepared to open the door? How do you open the door? It just occurred to me perhaps the Lord might be indicating something of the way we can open the door in John 14: 21, “He that has my commandments and keeps them, he it is that loves me; but he that loves me shall be loved by my Father, and I will love him and will manifest myself to him”. Do you believe that? If you believe it, have you ever experienced it? Have you ever experienced Jesus manifesting Himself to you?

He does not say, I will give him a manifestation, as though it were of something, but, I will manifest Myself to him. We may think that in days such as those in which we live that is not a possibility. What the Lord says is, “He that has my commandments and keeps them, he it is that loves me”. Do you love Him? He is very attractive; despite the world’s rejection of Him there is no Person so attractive as our glorious, adorable Lord. And it is as the power of His Person and His love grips your soul that you are prepared for the path of discipleship. Think of the compensation, “I will … manifest myself to him.”
In our passage He says, “I will … sup with him”. I wonder if I have experienced that, or if you have experienced that, “I will … sup with him”? He comes into our circumstances.

Would you be happy to invite Jesus to supper? And mark well that, despite what people may say, Jesus is particular who He eats with. Are you? The passage makes it clear. Oh, but you say, “This Man receives sinners and eats with them”, Luke 15: 2. Yes, but mark, He receives them first and eats with them. In the immediate context from which we are drawing He makes a condition—“If any one” or any man, that would include a woman too, a responsible person, “hear my voice”. Have you heard His voice? Have you heard His voice in the ministry? It is not only what He says, it is His voice. Can you detect His voice?

Beloved brethren, this awful departure from the light of God is very serious. Persons are rejecting the light of God that shone in the ministry of beloved James Taylor—it was the light of God. Was it from heaven, or was it of men? It was from heaven, and the light of God shone in it. It is being rejected by those who have been in the light of it—a solemn consideration. I would not be among them, I would like to hear His voice, His present speaking. You say, These men have gone. Yes, they have gone, but the Spirit of God has not gone. I make so bold as to repeat, more than Mr. Darby is here, and more than Mr. Raven is here, and more than Mr. Taylor is here; the Spirit of God is here in the assembly. The Lord is still interested and He still holds everything in His hand. He is still the Amen, He is still the faithful and true Witness, and He is prepared to come in and sup with you, subject to certain conditions.

He then says, “and he with me”. Would you not like to sup with the Lord in His circumstances and in His world? I would. I am quite sure of this, moreover, that when I got there I should not find myself the only guest at the table. But they would be selected guests.

Do you think the scripture justifies it? I am sure it does, because He makes the condition. So you do not find yourself alone there, although you have your own personal link with Him; you find others there also, supping with Him in His circumstances. No doubt there is a simple allusion to what may be available, without formally mentioning it, in the Lord’s supper. He comes to us where we are in our circumstances and takes us to where He is in His circumstances. That is present compensation in the testimony, not by-and-by. So He would encourage us, dear brethren, to go on. What are you going to do? Are you going on? Are you going to be among those that will be guests at His table, supping with Him? He maintains the service of God.
That brings me to the last part of His word, “He that overcomes, to him will I give to sit with me in my throne; as I also have overcome, and have sat down with my Father in his throne”.

Christ is there on His Father’s throne. He will soon take up His own, there is no doubt about it. A servant of the Lord once said, ‘Are you getting anxious about things? There will be time enough for me to get anxious when the Man on the throne gets anxious!’ He is not anxious; He is sustaining everything there for His Father; He is sustaining the testimony, and He is sustaining the service of God. It is not breaking down. What then is our simple part? In devotion and allegiance to Him to relate ourselves to Him as He moves forward in the testimony—not our testimony. It is not our testimony of the Lord, it is the testimony of our Lord. He is sustaining it all, dear brethren.

There is great room for encouragement, not depression, when we think of a word of counsel like this from Jesus, and the promises of Jesus. They are available in the darkest day, even in the day when because iniquity abounds the love of the most shall wax cold. What is proper to the assembly can be enjoyed by the faithful individual, but I believe the Lord always has the assembly in mind, and we do not find ourselves entirely alone. But we may in testimony find the circumstances very testing. Of course, they were for Him. Did you expect something different? If the Scripture tells me things will get worse, should I expect them to get better?

Hardly. It says, “Juggling impostors … leading and being led astray”, 2 Timothy 3: 13. If the Bible tells me that, let me believe it. But if the Lord promises something to the faithful individual, let me take courage and be faithful and prove His promise.

So will you accept a word of counsel from the Lord? It is His last word of counsel to the church and He would have us to lay hold of it. Dear brethren, when the truth is being shamelessly sold for material advantage, let us buy it and not sell it. Let us buy personally from Christ gold purified by fire; let us buy this white clothing, this clothing whereby we can have our part in the service of God and be rightly in His testimony; let us buy the eye-salve so that we may see and not be among those who either cannot, or do not want to see. Let us be among those who through personal devotion and deep exercise with Christ know what it is to receive things from Himself. The more we do that, the more we shall find ourselves together in the bond of the truth. That is the only bond. There is no other. You say, Does it not say that love is the bond of perfectness, Colossians 3: 14? That is perfectly true, but the truth is our bond here in a scene of contrariety.

May the Lord help us, dear brethren, may He give us courage to go on in the face of adversity until the day when He comes. He is coming, and things are not going to finish down here in poverty and decrepitude; that is not going to be the case. And the teaching that the church will be transferred to heaven because she has failed on earth is not the truth. The church will be transferred to heaven because she belongs there. And before the Lord comes, I believe, God will have something which in its nature and character is of the assembly. “And the Spirit and the bride say, Come”, Revelation 22: 17. Are you in the spirit of that? You young people have your life before you, I know. We have all been like that. I know what you think and say, It is all very well for you older people, with one foot in the grave, to talk like this about christianity.

Christianity, you know, is not just something to train the feet of toddlers, and comfort the ageing and the dying. Christianity and the testimony of God call for manhood, so that God’s testimony should be carried through in men and women who are of the order of Jesus Christ.

And you will find, young brothers and sisters, if you commit yourselves, however testing the circumstances, that Jesus is as good as His word: “I will come in unto him and sup with him, and he with me”. Set yourself for spiritual experiences with Him and He will not let you down. May the Lord bless every one of us, for His name’s sake.

articles.title: THE GRATING OF NETWORK IN THE ALTAR
articles.author: A. B. Parker

paragraphs.text: The “grating of network” in the altar of burnt-offering was made of copper. Apparently it would be under the offering, and the wood that was placed upon the altar. Only what was consumed by the fire on the altar could go through the network. There would be no lumps in the ashes that the priest removed from the altar; all had come through this grating, of network, indicating that there is to be nothing casual about the way matters are attended to.
Matters which arise amongst us are to be sorted out and
finished; they are to be completed. The Lord could say to Sardis, “I have not found thy works complete before my God”, Revelation 3: 2. Exercises are not to be left in abeyance unduly.

There can be no movement in the testimony if we do not complete matters; unless there is thorough self-judgment; unless our minds and hearts are in keeping with the heart of God in relation to moral issues, personal state, and general conditions in our localities. The altar, with the grating of network, should, in principle, be found in every locality.

I believe that the Lord, in ordering the terrible pressures which we have had to go through, involving loss of loved ones and brethren, has in mind that things are to be sorted out and purification accomplished. Where this is not done the compassions of God may be restrained, as suggested in the Lord being “girt about at the breasts with a golden girdle”, Revelation 1: 13. He is allowing the suffering to work out in us, and deepen the experience of self-judgment in the consciousness that God is holy, and those who draw near to Him must do so in righteousness and holiness. Therefore, matters must be gone into in detail and nothing lumpy or unfinished should be allowed to remain. The ashes taken from the altar and poured out in a clean place outside the camp suggest a public testimony that there is a sphere where
God dwells, where matters are thoroughly judged and worked out, providing a moral basis for the divine Presence to remain amongst us.
Dear brethren, if we are going to move on in the truth, as the Spirit of God is seeking to open it up to us in these days, we must be thorough in self-judgment individually and collectively.
I believe progress is being made, for as one moves around amongst the
brethren one finds an atmosphere conducive to increase, and a readiness and desire to take on the truth. The countenances of the brethren, too, show an appreciation of what the Spirit is bringing in.

Let us be characterised by what the copper suggests—a living, active judgment and repudiation of everything that is not of God. Nothing that is not of God should remain unjudged in the circle of fellowship, for if we do not deal with such things in such wise that the ashes go through the network, there can be no real spiritual progress, for the rings through which the staves were put to carry the altar were attached to the grating of network.

We have many types, of the Holy Spirit in Scripture. Some are fluid types, such as dew, water, wind, and oil. That is instructive, because we tend to become rigid and fixed in our minds, and this sometimes hinders the service and activity of the blessed Spirit. Everything has come to us in the Spirit, and the Spirit has come from heaven. The early chapters of the Acts are full of the thought of what is from heaven, and we need to be deepened in our apprehension

of what has come to us in the Spirit from heaven. The glad tidings also are preached in the power of the Spirit sent from heaven. He has come forth from with the Father, and He has been sent from with the Father, John 15: 26. That is how Jesus refers to the Comforter. But in any case what has come to us in this dispensation has come by the Spirit, and the Spirit has come from heaven. “A man can receive nothing”, John says, “unless it be given him out of heaven”, John 3: 27.

How much of that we have received is an interesting question for each of us. We can see that others received from heaven. Paul refers to what he received from the Lord, and the Lord was in heaven when Paul received it. Others received from the Lord, no doubt, when He was here upon earth—“for of his fulness we all have received, and grace upon grace”, John 1: 16. But

in regard to the glad tidings that he preached, Paul says he received them from the Lord. And in regard to the truth of the Lord’s supper, he says he received that from the Lord. These things have come to us in the Spirit sent down from heaven.

Now these two scriptures bring before us, firstly, the thought of what flows down, and, secondly, what returns in response springing up, “the water which I shall give him shall become in him a fountain of water, springing up into eternal life”. We thus have the descending thought and the ascending thought. Jesus it is who descended; not only from heaven did He come, but He descended into the lower parts of the earth from the lowly place He had already taken in the condition of manhood. He descended from that place—wondrous fact—into the lower parts of the earth. But “He that descended is the
same who has also ascended up above all the heavens”, Ephesians 4: 10. That is where He now is, and what has come from heaven in the Spirit has come from Him there.

This psalm is intended to arrest our thoughts. “Behold”, the word is, “how good and how pleasant it is for brethren to dwell together in unity!” There would be in that the true representation of God testimonially. Disunity is dishonouring to God. We should feel it deeply that God has been misrepresented through our failure. But the positiveness is in this thought of brethren dwelling together in unity. It is testimonial, I believe, according to what the Lord says to the Father, “That they may be one, as we are one … that the world may know that thou hast sent me”, John 17: 22, 23.

Then we are told that this dwelling together by brethren in unity is like “the precious oil upon the head, that ran down upon the beard, upon Aaron’s beard, that ran down to the hem of his garments”. That is a great comfort to me, dear brethren, that in this time, in this finishing time, the end of the dispensation, the Spirit of God is in no sense withdrawn from the divine side. He is here, in the assembly, right up to date “That ran down to the hem of his garments”;
“his garments” refer to what is here in relation to Christ. The hem is the finish; it is not a loose end, it is not something uncompleted. The hem of the garments is the completed thought.

God has great delight in what is complete. “My Father worketh hitherto and I work”, (John 5: 17), would be with a view to restful conditions being reached. God rested after His work which He had created; He rested on the seventh day. But then, the Lord says, “I have completed the work which thou gavest me that I should do it”, John 17: 11. And now, how can God’s work be complete if the Spirit of God is not made way for, made room for amongst us in every detail? I doubt whether there is anything we can do rightly, either in testimony or in serving God, without the Spirit.

Well, this condition of things is “like the precious oil”, and it is “as the dew … that descendeth”. We should be seized of this thought, dear brethren, of what comes down, the descending thought. Paul says, “Let this mind be in you which was also in Christ Jesus”, Philippians 2: 5. It is the tendency to go down which affords delight to heaven. Right from the outset in our souls’ relations with God as convicted sinners there should be with us the tendency to go down. “This man went down to his house justified rather than that other”, Luke 18: 14. It is not simply that he went to his house; he went down to it. What a time this is, beloved brethren, to be going down. We may review things which have come in on the public side—not to be unduly occupied with them, but just to promote a little more within each one of us the descending line. “The dew of Hermon that descendeth on the mountains of Zion; for there hath Jehovah commanded the blessing …” We are, I believe, assured as to where the Lord is, and we shall find that where He is the blessing is. “There hath Jehovah commanded the blessing”. That is a very choice thought—God commanding blessing! He may return, as the prophet says, and who knows but that He will leave a blessing behind Him, (see Joel 2: 14).

So He visits us today, here, in this place, and surely He will leave a blessing behind Him. But it says here that He commanded the blessing. Anything that is by divine command will stand. The truth of the mystery is by divine command, made known by commandment of the eternal God, (see Romans 16: 26). It is not something that Paul conceived in his mind. It was by revelation that he had it; and it was made known by commandment of the eternal God. Oh, dear brethren, we need to get hold of this thought of what is by divine command—“He spoke, and it was done; he commanded, and it stood fast” Psalm 33: 9.

So our present blessing is life for evermore. I suppose many of our fellow-believers think that they will go to heaven and enjoy eternal life there; but we shall not need it there. Eternal life is for the earth; it is for us now. It is to be known and enjoyed, and it is known and enjoyed by us now, in this scene of moral death. Mr. Raven said that if one says he has eternal life, he should be able to describe it. Could you describe what you have, in that sense? Well, I think, dear brethren, without going into doctrine, that we know the Lord has brought this about by divine command, life for evermore, and that it is for all to enjoy now. The blessing of eternal life is contained in the glad tidings, that they “may not perish, but have life eternal”, John 3: 16.
In John 4 we have eternal life again “a fountain of water, springing up into eternal life”. This involves what is from us towards God in His service, as the remainder of the passage shows.

The woman is led by the Lord quickly from this point into the great and wonderful realm of the worship of God. But first of all it is a question of the water that Christ would give; “The water which I shall give him shall become in him a fountain of water, springing up into eternal life”. The prophet Jeremiah (Jeremiah 2: 13) refers to “broken cisterns that can hold no water”. Every human system is a broken cistern.
There is no room in any human system for the Holy Spirit, and therefore no power to retain what is precious, what has come from heaven.
Now this woman was not a person like that; she was a vessel. She understands that she herself is a vessel. You can see that because she left her water-pot. She had become the

vessel. “Shall become in him a fountain of water, springing up into eternal life”—water, as we know, finds its own level. It rises to the level of its source. It cannot go beyond that, but it will do that. And so in the believer who has the Spirit there is that which rises up to God; it rises up to its Source, and it springs up. It has great energy behind it. Energy is to be expressed or manifested spiritually in the service of God in persons. Take the doxologies of Scripture; there you have it, springing up in those persons, extraordinary persons. Take a man like Nebuchadnezzar, once unconverted; “Whom he would he slew, and whom he would he kept alive”, Daniel 5: 19. But God put out His hand and reached that man and made him personally a vessel of praise. So we have a doxology from the lips of a man like Nebuchadnezzar, “Now I Nebuchadnezzar praise and extol and honour the King of the heavens, all whose works are truth, and his paths judgment”, Daniel 4: 37. Then there are Paul and others in the New Testament—springing up into eternal life are their doxologies.

They could not have been premeditated; they were spontaneous. The Lord has great regard for what is spontaneous in each one of us, and more especially in the assembly where there is the responsive springing up of affection for Christ and in the service of God.

So I thought it would move our hearts, dear brethren, to see, on the one hand, what descends, what has come to us in the Spirit, as alone it could in divine light and love, direct from God into our souls. But it is not merely to be left there, but to return in mighty response as Paul says, “To him be glory in the assembly in Christ Jesus unto all generations of the age of ages. Amen”, Ephesians 3: 21
INSTINCTS

It was a late June morning in the North of Scotland when we saw a tiny fledgling swift resting on a window ledge. It was quite motionless, perhaps tired after its first flight. The miracle is that by early August that bird—having left Britain in advance of its parents—will be winging its way on the 5000 to 7000 mile journey to its winter home in southern Africa. By what means? By God-given instinct. The God who has given birds such amazing instincts has also given spiritual instincts to His children. As the work of God begins, certain instincts are implanted. As that work proceeds, and the Holy Spirit is received, they become deeper and stronger. It is vital to our preservation in the christian way that we remain true to those instincts. They will help in many situations. They may tell me that the books I read are damaging; that the company I keep is not suitable; that certain teaching is not in accord with the truth. Thus there is salvation in heeding right instincts and not stifling them.
Mr. Taylor made the striking statement, “Very often instinct is truer in us than intelligence”

(N.S. Vol. 31, p.124). One looks back on circumstances in which if one had been true to instinct it would have meant preservation from damage and loss. May the Lord help us to be submissive to the inward senses that God has given, so that we may be kept from evil and preserved in the course in which we shall prove His blessing and protection.
